metadata.query: What happened between Verstappen and Hamilton at Turn 4 during the 2021 Brazilian GP, and why did the stewards not penalize it?

data.query: What happened between Verstappen and Hamilton at Turn 4 during the 2021 Brazilian GP, and why did the stewards not penalize it?
data.summary:
### The Incident (Lap 48 — November 14, 2021)
During Lap 48 of the 2021 São Paulo (Brazilian) Grand Prix, Lewis Hamilton attempted to overtake Max Verstappen around the outside of Turn 4 [1.2]. Verstappen, defending the inside line, braked very late and ran wide [1.2]. This action forced both cars completely off the track and onto the asphalt run-off area [1.2, 1.3]. Verstappen remained ahead to retain the lead [1.2]. 

### Why the Stewards Did Not Penalize It
The FIA Race Director, Michael Masi, and the stewards chose not to investigate or penalize the move during the race due to the following reasons [1.2, 1.3]:

1. **The "Let Them Race" Principle:** Masi explained that the stewards applied the overarching "let them race" philosophy [1.2, 1.3]. This was an agreed-upon approach among teams, drivers, and the FIA to encourage hard, discretionary wheel-to-wheel racing [1.2].
2. **No Contact or Change in Position:** The stewards assessed that both cars went off-track, neither car made contact with the other, and neither driver lost or gained a position relative to each other (Verstappen stayed ahead, and Hamilton remained second) [1.2, 1.3].
3. **Lack of On-board Footage:** During their live deliberation, the stewards did not have access to Verstappen’s forward-facing onboard camera, as it was not part of the live broadcast feed and had to be downloaded after the race [1.2, 1.3]. They decided at the time that they had sufficient broadcast angles to make a quick ruling of no further action [1.2, 1.6].

### Post-Race "Right of Review" Rejection (November 19, 2021)
Following the race, Mercedes submitted a petition for a **Right of Review** under Article 14 of the FIA International Sporting Code (ISC) once Verstappen's onboard footage was publicly released [1.2, 1.6]. 

On November 19, 2021, the stewards denied the request [1.2]. While they acknowledged that the onboard footage was "new" and "relevant," they ruled it was not "significant" enough to overturn their initial in-race discretionary decision, stating that they saw no reason to retrospecitvely penalize a move that both drivers ultimately resolved on-track [1.2, 1.6] (with Hamilton eventually overtaking Verstappen on Lap 59 to win the race) [1.2].

2. **No Contact or Change in Position:** The stewards assessed that both cars went off-track, neither car made contact with the other, and neither driver lost or gained a position relative to each other (Verstappen stayed ahead, and Hamilton remained second) [1.2, 1.3].
